section_summary: This section covers U.S. State Department correspondence, intelligence reports, and SCAP records concerning religious affairs in occupied Japan from January 1945 to April 1947. Key topics include U.S. policy on religious freedom, the disestablishment of State Shinto, the visit of an American Protestant church deputation, and Vatican requests regarding Catholic properties in Japan. Additional reports examine wartime Christian church conditions, Communist and Buddhist political attitudes, and geopolitical tensions surrounding Soviet efforts to influence the Japanese Orthodox Church.

subfiles.about: An American soldier of Japanese ancestry urges a Christian religious program for post-war Japan and Japanese prisoners of war.
subfiles.summary: Kumataka inquires whether a religious program is planned to bring Christianity to Japan and war prisoners, volunteering his services.
subfiles.title: Letter to the President regarding Christian work in Japan

subfiles.about: Suggests draft language for replying to Wilson Kumataka regarding religious freedom in post-war Japan and jurisdiction over POWs.
subfiles.from: B. R. Johansen (Division of Japanese Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Recommends replying that post-war Japan will have religious freedom and referring POW religious inquiries to the Provost Marshal General.
subfiles.title: Reply to Mr. Kumataka's letter of January 6 to the President

subfiles.about: Transmits letter concerning Kumataka for instructions or a copy of reply for precedent use.
subfiles.from: M. V. Trent (Division of Public Liaison)
subfiles.summary: Forwards attached letter for instructions or a copy of the reply for precedent files.
subfiles.title: Transmittal of letter concerning Mr. Kumataka
subfiles.to: Erle R. Dickover (Division of Japanese Affairs)

subfiles.about: Official State Department reply explaining U.S. hopes for post-war religious freedom in Japan and referring POW matters to the War Department.
subfiles.from: J. M. Colton Hand (Division of Public Liaison)
subfiles.summary: States U.S. commitment to religious freedom in post-war Japan and refers POW inquiries to the Provost Marshal General.
subfiles.title: Letter to Wilson Kumataka regarding religious life in Japan

subfiles.about: Quotes 19th-century scholars J. J. Rein and W. E. Griffis on the historical evolution and decline of Shintoism and Mikado deification.
subfiles.from: Erle R. Dickover (Office of Far Eastern Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Quotes J. J. Rein and W. E. Griffis to demonstrate the pitfalls of dogmatic assertions regarding Shintoism and the Mikado.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on dogmatic assertions concerning Shintoism and the Mikado

subfiles.about: Transmits an Osservatore Romano report on the safety of Catholic missionaries and atomic bomb casualties in Hiroshima and Nagasaki.
subfiles.from: Harold H. Tittmann (Assistant to Myron C. Taylor, Vatican City)
subfiles.summary: Reports Vatican news confirming interned Catholic missionaries are safe and that the bishops of Nagasaki and Hiroshima survived bombings abroad.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-39: Report on Catholic Missions in Japan

subfiles.about: Transmits a Vatican note requesting exemption of undamaged Catholic churches and schools in Japan from military requisition.
subfiles.from: Harold H. Tittmann (Assistant to Myron C. Taylor, Vatican City)
subfiles.summary: Transmits a Holy See note verbale requesting Allied occupation authorities exempt surviving Catholic churches and schools from requisition.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 444: Request from the Holy See that Catholic Churches and Schools in Japan be exempted from requisition

subfiles.about: Comments on Catholic Church requests regarding property in Japan, arguing against acquiescing to demands.
subfiles.summary: Argues against granting special property protections to the Catholic Church in Japan, noting Japan is not a Catholic country.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Catholic Church requests regarding Japanese properties
subfiles.to: Albert E. Clattenburg (Special War Problems Division)

subfiles.about: Outlines Allied military policy in Italy regarding requisitioning Catholic and religious property for comparative background.
subfiles.summary: Explains Allied policy in Italy avoided requisitioning Catholic properties, but notes religious circumstances differ in non-Catholic countries.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Allied military policy regarding church property in Italy

subfiles.about: Instructs Tittmann on replying to the Holy See's request concerning Catholic property and personnel in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Returns Vatican note and provides copies of communications to the Papal Delegate and Secretary of War to guide response.
subfiles.title: Instruction to Harold H. Tittmann regarding Catholic property in Japan

subfiles.about: Reports Japanese press sensation over Vincent's broadcast on abolishing State Shinto and requests clarification.
subfiles.summary: Reports intense Japanese public interest following Vincent's broadcast on abolishing State Shinto and requests telegraphic details.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 36 regarding Vincent's broadcast on State Shinto

subfiles.about: Clarifies U.S. policy separating State Shinto from individual religious practice and ending government support for Shinto.
subfiles.summary: Clarifies that individual Shinto worship will not be disturbed, but State Shinto, public funding, and militaristic ideology will end.
subfiles.title: Outgoing telegram to SCAP regarding Vincent's broadcast on Shinto

subfiles.about: Transmits travel applications for the four Protestant churchmen visiting Japan and urges high travel priority.
subfiles.from: A. L. Warnshuis (Federal Council of Churches)
subfiles.summary: Submits travel applications for the four-man church deputation to Japan, emphasizing the urgency of rapid transport arrangements.
subfiles.title: Letter transmitting travel applications for Protestant deputation

subfiles.about: Transmits a $5,000 certified check to be exchanged for yen to cover living and travel expenses of the deputation in Japan.
subfiles.from: A. L. Warnshuis (Federal Council of Churches)
subfiles.summary: Transmits a certified check for $5,000 to be disbursed in yen in Tokyo for deputation living and transportation expenses.
subfiles.title: Letter transmitting check for expenses of Protestant deputation
subfiles.to: Office of the Fiscal Director (War Department)

subfiles.about: Endorses the visit of the American Protestant deputation to confer with Japanese Christians and quotes MacArthur on spiritual reconstruction.
subfiles.summary: Endorses the Protestant church deputation to Japan, citing General MacArthur on the fundamental theological need for spiritual reconstruction.
subfiles.title: Letter endorsing Protestant deputation to Japan

subfiles.about: Requests a presidential letter of commendation for the four Protestant leaders traveling to Japan, citing Roosevelt's earlier letter.
subfiles.from: A. L. Warnshuis (Federal Council of Churches)
subfiles.summary: Informs President Truman of the four-man Protestant deputation to Japan and requests a letter of personal interest and good wishes.
subfiles.title: Letter requesting presidential letter of support for deputation

subfiles.about: Commends Warnshuis's 1944 mission to England and Europe regarding post-war church rehabilitation.
subfiles.summary: Expresses presidential support for Dr. Warnshuis's 1944 mission to England and Europe to rehabilitate post-war spiritual work.
subfiles.title: Letter of commendation for European church mission

subfiles.about: State Department draft of the President's endorsement letter for the Protestant deputation to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Draft presidential reply commending the Protestant deputation to Japan and citing MacArthur's statement on spiritual character.
subfiles.title: Draft presidential letter to Douglas Horton

subfiles.about: Outlines the background, purpose, personnel, and itinerary of the four-man Protestant deputation to Japan.
subfiles.from: A. L. Warnshuis (Chairman, Committee on Arrangements)
subfiles.summary: Details the background, personnel, and objectives of the four-man Protestant deputation sent to restore fellowship with Japanese Christians.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Concerning the Proposed Visit to Japan of a Deputation representing the Protestant Churches in America

subfiles.about: Transmits a copy of the letter sent to the War Department Fiscal Director regarding the $5,000 deputation funds.
subfiles.summary: Transmits to Lory a copy of the letter sent to the War Department Fiscal Director regarding funds.
subfiles.title: Letter transmitting copy of War Department fiscal letter

subfiles.about: Reports the departure of the four churchmen from San Francisco via United Air Lines and expresses gratitude for State Department assistance.
subfiles.summary: Confirms departure of the four churchmen from San Francisco for Tokyo and thanks Lory for his efficient assistance.
subfiles.title: Letter reporting departure of church deputation for Japan

subfiles.about: Inquires about official channels and permissions for shipping Japanese and Korean Scriptures to Japan and Korea.
subfiles.summary: Offers donation of Japanese and Korean Scriptures and inquires about official channels and shipping clearances.
subfiles.title: Letter regarding shipment of Bibles to Japan and Korea

subfiles.about: Refers the American Bible Society to the War Department Civil Affairs Division for shipping clearances.
subfiles.summary: Advises the American Bible Society to contact the Civil Affairs Division of the War Department for Bible shipments.
subfiles.title: Reply regarding shipment of Bibles to Japan and Korea

subfiles.about: Transmits a detailed memorandum by Russell L. Durgin analyzing Christian churches, schools, and property damage in Japan during and after World War II.
subfiles.from: John S. Service / George Atcheson, Jr. (Office of the U.S. Political Adviser, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Transmits Russell L. Durgin's comprehensive study of the wartime condition and post-war revival of Christian churches in Japan. The report reviews government control under the 1939 Religious Bodies Law, the persecution of Holiness Church pastors, changes in Christian schools, church property destruction, and Japanese views regarding the return of foreign missionaries.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 111: Christian Churches in Japan During the War

subfiles.about: Transmits a memorandum by Russell L. Durgin and an interview by Father Patrick O'Connor with Communist leader Sanzo Nosaka.
subfiles.from: George Atcheson, Jr. (Office of the U.S. Political Adviser, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: Presents an intelligence survey and exclusive interview regarding Japanese Communist ideology toward religion. Communist leaders Kyuichi Tokuda and Sanzo Nosaka characterize religion as an opiate of the people to be eliminated under socialism. Nosaka details party strategy, coalitional politics, and educational and land-reform policies.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 374: Attitude of Japanese Communists Toward Religion

subfiles.about: Internal State Department routing slip distributing copies of document.
subfiles.summary: Designates internal routing and distribution of copies to Far Eastern, War, and Navy offices.
subfiles.title: DC/R Routing Slip

subfiles.about: Transmits a memorandum by Russell L. Durgin on political engagement of Christians, Shinto sects, and Buddhists, with a statement by Riri Nakayama.
subfiles.summary: Surveys the political involvement of Japanese religious groups in the 1946 general election. While religious leaders largely favor moral influence over partisan politics, several Shinto sects and a Buddhist Party nominated candidates. The report includes an essay by Buddhist priest Riri Nakayama advocating moral oversight rather than pursuit of governmental power.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 382: Political Activities of Japanese Religious Groups

subfiles.about: Advises that Bishop Tucker has postponed his trip to Japan until the fall.
subfiles.summary: Relays notification that Episcopal Bishop Tucker has postponed his visit to Japan until autumn.
subfiles.title: Telegram Z 33258: Postponement of Bishop Tucker's trip

subfiles.about: Forwards new missionary policy for Japan pursuant to telephone conversation.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the new missionary policy for Japan pursuant to an earlier telephone conversation.
subfiles.title: Routing note on new missionary policy for Japan

subfiles.about: Transmittal sheets for incoming clear messages filed under 894.404/11-2646.
subfiles.summary: War Department Classified Message Center incoming clear message form sheets filed under decimal number 894.404/11-2646.
subfiles.title: War Department incoming clear messages regarding Japan

subfiles.about: Records discussion with John Carter Vincent recommending clearance for Mrs. Sasaki's visit to assist Japanese Buddhist reorganization.
subfiles.from: Gordon T. Bowles (Division of Occupied Areas Economic Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Recommends approving Mrs. Sasaki's trip to Japan to assist Buddhist organizations with democratic reorganization and occupation policies.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation: Approval of Trip of Mrs. Sasaki to Japan

subfiles.about: Reports concern by Russian Orthodox Church Abroad leaders in Munich over Soviet influence if Moscow appoints the Tokyo archbishop.
subfiles.summary: Reports Munich Russian Orthodox leaders fear a Moscow appointment to Tokyo would result in Soviet domination of the Japanese congregation.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 2831: Russian Orthodox Archbishop for Tokyo

subfiles.about: Quotes a Tass report alleging MacArthur forced an American Orthodox bishop on Japan and asks SCAP for comments.
subfiles.summary: Requests SCAP comments on a Tass dispatch alleging MacArthur unconstitutionally imposed an American bishop and barred Patriarch Alexius.
subfiles.title: Outgoing telegram to SCAP regarding Tass report on Orthodox bishop appointment

subfiles.about: Provides chronological refutation of Tass allegations, explaining Japanese Orthodox congregation's request for an American bishop and resistance to Soviet pressure.
subfiles.summary: Refutes Tass allegations, detailing how the Japanese Orthodox Church democratically requested an American bishop (Bishop Benjamin) and resisted Soviet infiltration.
subfiles.title: Unnumbered telegram from Tokyo regarding Orthodox Church controversy

subfiles.about: Transmits text of SCAP's February 1 telegram regarding the Japanese Orthodox Church and exclusion of the Moscow Patriarch's envoy.
subfiles.summary: Transmits SCAP's telegram refuting Tass claims concerning the appointment of an Orthodox bishop in Japan to the Moscow mission.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 1850: Transmitting Tokyo telegram on Orthodox Church to Moscow Mission
